ddl:
CREATE TABLE User (
    Address VARCHAR(255),
    Birthday DATETIME,
    Current_location VARCHAR(255),
    Email VARCHAR(255),
    Gender VARCHAR(255),
    Hometown VARCHAR(255),
    Interests VARCHAR(255),
    Motto VARCHAR(255),
    Name VARCHAR(255),
    Password VARCHAR(255),
    Personal_profile VARCHAR(255),
    Phone VARCHAR(255),
    Relationship_status VARCHAR(255),
    User_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    User_type VARCHAR(255),
    Username VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE User_homepage (
    Creation_time DATETIME,
    Homepage_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Introduction VARCHAR(255),
    Title VARCHAR(255),
    User_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (User_ID) REFERENCES User(User_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE User_connection_request_record (
    Receiver_user_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Record_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Send_time DATETIME,
    Sender_user_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (Receiver_user_ID) REFERENCES User(User_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Sender_user_ID) REFERENCES User(User_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE User_connection_establishment_record (
    Connection_time DATETIME,
    Receiver_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Record_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Sender_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (Receiver_ID) REFERENCES User(User_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Sender_ID) REFERENCES User(User_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Feed (
    Feed_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Feed_content VARCHAR(255),
    Homepage_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Post_time DATETIME,
    User_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (Homepage_ID) REFERENCES User_homepage(Homepage_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (User_ID) REFERENCES User(User_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE User_homepage_join (
    Homepage_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Join_time DATETIME,
    User_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Join_time, Homepage_ID, User_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Homepage_ID) REFERENCES User_homepage(Homepage_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (User_ID) REFERENCES User(User_ID)
);
gold_question: Description of Social Network System Requirements: For user registration and login, users can register and log in to the system using username and password. The system supports different types of users, such as regular users and administrators. For personal information management, users can fill in and manage basic personal information, including name, phone, address, email, birthday, gender, relationship status, interests, etc., and can edit detailed information such as personal profile, motto, hometown, and current location. For user connection management, users can establish connections with other users, and the system records the connection time. Users can send and receive connection requests, and the system records the request sending time. For user homepage management, users can create personal homepages, including title, introduction, and creation time. Other users can join user's homepage and the joining time is recorded. For homepage feed management, users can post updates on their own homepage, including text content, and the posting time is recorded. Other users can also post updates on user's homepage, creating interaction. For the functionality of users joining multiple homepages, users can join multiple different homepages, and the joining time is recorded. The system supports associations between users and multiple homepages.
nl_text: The database name is rschema_0333, and it contains six tables. The first table, User, has the following columns: Address, Birthday, Current_location, Email, Gender, Hometown, Interests, Motto, Name, Password, Personal_profile, Phone, Relationship_status, User_ID (primary key), User_type, and Username. The second table, User_homepage, has the following columns: Creation_time, Homepage_ID (primary key), Introduction, Title, User_ID (foreign key referencing User), and Feed_ID (foreign key referencing Feed). The third table, User_connection_request_record, has the following columns: Receiver_user_ID (foreign key referencing User), Record_ID (primary key), Send_time, Sender_user_ID (foreign key referencing User). The fourth table, User_connection_establishment_record, has the following columns: Connection_time, Receiver_ID (foreign key referencing User), Record_ID (primary key), Sender_ID (foreign key referencing User). The fifth table, Feed, has the following columns: Feed_ID (primary key), Feed_content, Homepage_ID (foreign key referencing User_homepage), Post_time, and User_ID (foreign key referencing User). The sixth table, User_homepage_join, has the following columns: Homepage_ID (foreign key referencing User_homepage), Join_time, User_ID (foreign key referencing User), and PRIMARY KEY (Join_time, Homepage_ID, User_ID).
